Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-28 16:00 UTC
Duration: 37 minutes
Attendees: Jared Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Anita Zhao (Redwood CSM) - Marta Reyes (Auric), Liam O'Connor (Auric), Sofia Mendez (Auric)

Summary (auto): quick renewal check-in focused on capacity bump (2x), adding Ireland region for EU residency, and contract extension timing. Discussed pilot plan (Dedicated in IE), compliance docs, and benchmark data requirements.

Topics: renewal timeline, capacity sizing, dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs, VPC/on-prem constraints, SOC2/KMS, pilot test plan, next steps and owners.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jared: hey everyone, thanks for joining — we'll do a quick 30 minute run through, agenda is renewal sizing, eu region, and next steps. you all good with that?
[00:08] Marta: yep, sounds good. short on time so appreciate it.
[00:12] Priya: quick intro from me — i'm priya on the systems engineering side, i'll own the pilot and benchmarks.
[00:17] Liam: liam, platform eng, i'll pull the traffic and coordinate infra.
[00:20] Sofia: sofia — security. i'll need to confirm KMS details and audit scope.
[00:24] Jared: cool. high level from auric: you're at about 1.2B tokens/mo today on hosted, expect to double during Q1 as new fraud models roll out, is that still the plan marta?
[00:33] Marta: yeah that's right. we want predictable performance and lower p99 latency. hosting costs are creeping up so we want to lock in a better unit rate and add an IE region for data residency.
[00:43] Jared: totally. main options we've discussed: 1) hosted API add regional routing (fastest), 2) Dedicated reserved capacity with eu(ie) pool, or 3) Private VPC/on-prem for strict residency. it sounded like you want dedicated in ireland as a middle ground?
[00:58] Marta: correct. Hosted doesn't meet our residency controls; private on-prem is heavy for this phase. dedicated with VPC peering would work if we can get the SLA on latency and a price break for commit.
[01:12] Priya: couple notes on the engineering side — Dedicated gives you consistent throughput and KV cache locality which helps p99. we can co-locate model variants in the IE pool to avoid cross-region KV misses. Micro-batching can reduce cost but increases tail latency, so we need to tune batch windows for your 95th percentile targets.
[01:32] Liam: can you remind me, priya, about the KV cache mis — like does the cache replicate across geos? we want to avoid heavy cross-region egress.
[01:40] Priya: good q — for Dedicated we keep per-geocluster KV so as long as we stage model and prefix data in IE it stays local. the fallback policy will route to hosted/us if capacity exhausted, but we can restrict fallback for data residency. there was a little audio drop there — sorry if i said 'kay vee cache' odd.
[01:58] Sofia: on compliance — SOC2 type 2 is fine, we need to validate KMS integration with our AWS HSM. do you support customer-managed keys and bring-your-own-key flows? we need audit logs at token level for 90 days.
[02:11] Jared: yes, customer KMS is supported in Private and Dedicated flows; hosted supports CMEK for certain tiers. audit logs are available, retention tiers vary; we'll share the SOC2 and audit export doc after this call.
[02:23] Marta: about price — what's the rough per-token delta if we move to Dedicated with 2x capacity?
[02:28] Jared: i'll send the worksheet, but ballpark, commit discounts kick in at the reserved level — you should see 20-30% per-token reduction at 2x commit versus pay-as-you-go hosted, depending on model mix and quantization.
[02:41] Liam: model mix — we're mostly using open Llama variants and a smaller custom reranker. any gotchas on quantized models?
[02:48] Priya: quantization works fine; we recommend 4-bit profiles for the reranker too, but there's a quality tradeoff we'll validate in the pilot. the runtime will pick kernels differently, so we'll run the same inference traces to confirm latency. oops, just cut a word there — 'kernels' got transcribed as 'carnels' sometimes in older notes.
[03:05] Marta: timeline — our procurement only meets first week of jan, but we'd like pilot before the end of january so we can include results in the renewal amendment. thoughts?
[03:15] Jared: feasible. proposed plan: get traffic sample by 12/31, Redwood runs a 1-week Dedicated pilot in IE during first full week of jan, then produce benchmark report and a draft contract amendment by Jan 11. That hits procurement meeting.
[03:29] Sofia: pilot — will there be data plane access or is it just synthetic load? we need to ensure no PHI is exposed to Redwood in logs.
[03:36] Priya: pilot can be run with sanitized samples and you can host the traffic in a peered VPC; we can sign an SCP to avoid retention of raw inputs beyond temp. also we can run a local perf-only mode where we don't store payloads.
[03:47] Liam: ok i'll sanitize and provide IP allowlist. any special headers we should include to route to IE?
[03:52] Priya: we'll provide endpoint and routing headers; also we'll share a quickstart and a test harness that simulates your peak distribution.
[03:58] Marta: how does fallback and failover look if IE pool hits capacity during peak?
[04:02] Jared: we propose policy: no cross-region fallback for regulated routes (so request fails if capacity exceeded) and allow non-regulated routes to fall back to hosted. we can also configure burst capacity for a short window — that's an add-on but useful.
[04:16] Sofia: bursting to hosted is a no-go for residency routes; we might allow queued requests or 429s. we'll document that in the audit.
[04:23] Priya: noted. we'll show both policies in the pilot and measure SLO impact.
[04:27] Liam: about SLA — p99 target? currently we want sub-250ms p99 for the shortest path. is that realistic with batching and reranker?
[04:35] Priya: for generation models under 512 tokens, sub-250ms p99 is tight but achievable with Dedicated, optimized kernels, and KV locality. reranker latency is small but depends on input size. we'll validate in pilot; if not, we can propose a p99-SLO with a higher commit.
[04:50] Marta: procurement will push on financials — do you have a templated amendment for +capacity and region add?
[04:56] Jared: yes, we'll attach an amendment template to the pricing worksheet. it includes term length, commit level, regions, and SLAs.
[05:03] Sofia: encryption at rest, in transit? and do you support SAML for SSO and fine-grained RBAC?
[05:09] Jared: yes — TLS in transit and AES-256 at rest; SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning, role-based RBAC are standard on enterprise tiers. we'll include the SAML metadata and RBAC model in the security pack.
[05:19] Marta: great. quick question — competitors: we've done talks with MajorCloudAI and VerticaServe; pricing similar but their eu options were slower. anything we should call out to procurement as differentiator?
[05:29] Jared: highlight production-first tooling: token-level cost dashboards, built-in KV cache controls, and transparent kernel/quantization guidance. plus our rollouts allow canary to dedicated without code changes.
[05:40] Priya: i'd add that our benchmark harness ties regressions to eval prompts so quality changes are caught during rollouts, which saves time for model ops.
[05:49] Liam: sweet. for the benchmark, does Redwood need live auth tokens or can we use a short-lived API key?
[05:55] Priya: short-lived API key should be fine; if you want VPC peering we'll coordinate network config.
[05:59] Marta: ok let's capture next steps.
[06:01] Jared: recap — liam to send 48h sanitized traffic by 12/31; priya to propose pilot slots and test plan by 12/30; jared to send pricing worksheet, soc2 and KMS notes by Jan 2; sofia to confirm KMS/HSM constraints and audit scope by Jan 4; follow-up meeting Jan 11 to finalize amendment.
[06:20] Anita: i'll add notes to the renewal tracker and cc procurement.
[06:24] Marta: one last ask — can we get a sample SLA report from a previous dedicated deployment? procurement likes a readout.
[06:30] Jared: yes i'll anonymize an SLA report and include with the security pack.
[06:33] Sofia: cool. thanks everyone.
[06:35] Jared: thanks all, we'll follow up in threads. bye.

End of call.

Notes on transcription quality: minor word swaps (kv pronounced as "kay vee", "kernels" misheard as "carnels" in one spot), occasional overlapping talk, timestamps approximate.
